The words

Raise your triumphant songs
To an immortal tune,
Let the wide earth resound the deeds
Celestial grace has done.

Sing how eternal love
Its chief beloved chose,
And bid him raise our wretched race
From their abyss of woes.

His hand no thunder bears,
Nor terror clothes his brow,
No bolts to drive our guilty souls
To fiercer flames below.

'Twas mercy fill'd the throne,
And wrath stood silent by,
When Christ was sent with pardons down
To rebels doom'd to die.

Now, sinners, dry your tears,
Let hopeless sorrow cease;
Bow to the sceptre of his love,
And take the offer'd peace.

Lord we obey thy call;
We lay an humble claim
To the salvation thou hast brought,
And love and praise thy Name.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Bb and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on l, (G), on the word “Raise”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 104, headed “The same”.

Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.

  • Words (1707): Isaac Watts (1674–1748)
  • Music (1762): Samuel Howard (died undefined)

Tune ST. BRIDE by Samuel Howard (died undefined); words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748).

Questions about Raise Your Triumphant Songs

What is the doh of Raise Your Triumphant Songs?

In this version, in G minor, doh is Bb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Raise Your Triumphant Songs start on?

It starts on l, (G in G minor), a pickup on the word “Raise” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to l,.

Is Raise Your Triumphant Songs in the public domain?

Yes. Isaac Watts died in 1748, Samuel Howard died in undefined; the words were first published in 1707 and the music in 1762. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
